readings.title: The Golden Calf
readings.subtitle: A Great Sin Against YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Exodus 32:1] And when the people saw that Mosheh was so long in coming down from the mountain, the people gathered together to Aharon, and said to him, “Rise up, make us mighty ones who go before us. For this Mosheh, the man who brought us up out of the land of Mitsrayim, we do not know what has become of him.” [2] And Aharon said to them, “Break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.” [3] And all the people broke off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them to Aharon. [4] And he took this from their hand, and formed it with an engraving tool, and made a moulded calf. And they said, “This is your mighty one, O Yisra’ĕl, that brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim!” [5] And Aharon saw it, and built an altar before it. And Aharon called out and said, “Tomorrow is a festival to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [6] And they rose early on the next day, and offered ascending offerings, and brought peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Go, get down! For your people whom you brought out of the land of Mitsrayim have corrupted themselves.</dq> [8] <dq>“They have turned aside quickly out of the way which <dn>I</dn> commanded them. They have made themselves a moulded calf, and bowed themselves to it and slaughtered to it, and said, ‘This is your mighty one, O Yisra’ĕl, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim!’ ”</dq> [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have seen this people, and see, it is a stiff-necked people!</dq> [10] <dq>“And now, let <dn>Me</dn> alone, that <dn>My</dn> wrath might burn against them and <dn>I</dn> consume them and <dn>I</dn> make of you a great nation.”</dq> [11] And Mosheh pleaded with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>, and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, why does <dn>Your</dn> wrath burn against <dn>Your</dn> people whom <dn>You</dn> have brought out of the land of Mitsrayim with great power and with a strong hand? [12] “Why should the Mitsrites speak, and say, ‘<dn>He</dn> brought them out for evil, to kill them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth’? Turn from the heat of <dn>Your</dn> wrath, and relent from this evil to <dn>Your</dn> people. [13] “Remember Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Yisra’ĕl, <dn>Your</dn> servants, to whom <dn>You</dn> swore by <dn>Yourself</dn>, and said to them, ‘<dn>I</dn> increase your seed like the stars of the heavens. And all this land that <dn>I</dn> have spoken of <dn>I</dn> give to your seed, and they shall inherit it forever.’ ” [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> relented concerning the evil which <dn>He</dn> said <dn>He</dn> would do to <dn>His</dn> people. [15] And Mosheh turned and went down from the mountain, and the two tablets of the Witness were in his hand, tablets written on both their sides, written on the one side and on the other. [16] And the tablets were the work of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the writing was the writing of <dn>Elohim</dn> engraved on the tablets. [17] And Yehoshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, and he said to Mosheh, “A noise of battle in the camp!” [18] But he said, “It is not the sound of a shout of might, nor is it the sound of a cry of defeat, but the sound of singing I hear.” [19] And it came to be, as soon as he came near the camp, that he saw the calf and the dancing. And Mosheh’s wrath burned, and he threw the tablets out of his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain. [20] And he took the calf which they had made, and burned it in the fire, and ground it into powder, and scattered it on the water and made the children of Yisra’ĕl drink it. [21] And Mosheh said to Aharon, “What did this people do to you that you have brought so great a sin upon them?” [22] And Aharon said, “Do not let the wrath of my master burn. You know the people, that it is in evil. [23] “And they said to me, ‘Make us mighty ones who go before us. For this Mosheh, the man who brought us up out of the land of Mitsrayim, we do not know what has become of him.’ [24] “And I said to them, ‘Whoever has any gold, let them break it off.’ So they gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.” [25] And Mosheh saw that the people were let loose, for Aharon had let them loose, to their shame among their enemies. [26] And Mosheh stood in the entrance of the camp, and said, “Who is for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Come to me.” And all the sons of Lewi gathered themselves to him. [27] And he said to them, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Let every man put his sword on his side, and pass over to and fro from gate to gate in the camp, and let every man kill his brother, and every man his friend, and every man his neighbour.’ ” [28] And the sons of Lewi did according to the word of Mosheh. And about three thousand men of the people fell that day. [29] And Mosheh said, “You are ordained for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> today – since every man has been against his son and against his brother – so as to bring upon you a blessing today.”

readings.title: Intercession and Separation
readings.subtitle: The Tent Outside the Camp
readings.text: [Exodus 32:30] And it came to be on the next day that Mosheh said to the people, “You have sinned a great sin. And now I am going up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – if I might atone for your sin.” [31] And Mosheh returned to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “Oh, these people have sinned a great sin, and have made for themselves a mighty one of gold! [32] “And now, if <dn>You</dn> would forgive their sin, but if not, please blot me out of <dn>Your</dn> book which <dn>You</dn> have written.” [33] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Whoever has sinned against <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> blot him out of <dn>My</dn> book.</dq> [34] <dq>“And now, go, lead the people to the place of which <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you. See, <dn>My</dn> Messenger goes before you. And in the day of <dn>My</dn> visitation <dn>I</dn> shall visit their sin upon them.”</dq> [35] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> plagued the people because of what they did with the calf which Aharon made. [Exodus 33:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Go, go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought out of the land of Mitsrayim, to the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Yaʽaqoḇ, saying, ‘To your seed <dn>I</dn> give it.’</dq> [2] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>My</dn> Messenger before you, and <dn>I</dn> shall drive out the Kenaʽanite and the Amorite and the Ḥittite and the Perizzite and the Ḥiwwite and the Yeḇusite,</dq> [3] <dq>“to a land flowing with milk and honey. For <dn>I</dn> do not go up in your midst because you are a stiff-necked people, lest <dn>I</dn> consume you on the way.”</dq> [4] And when the people heard this evil word, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments. [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Say to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. Should <dn>I</dn> go up in your midst for one moment <dn>I</dn> shall consume you. And now, take off your ornaments, and <dn>I</dn> shall know what to do to you.’ ”</dq> [6] So the children of Yisra’ĕl took off their ornaments at Mount Ḥorĕḇ. [7] And Mosheh took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and called it the Tent of Meeting. And it came to be that everyone who sought <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went out to the Tent of Meeting which was outside the camp. [8] And it came to be, whenever Mosheh went out to the Tent, that all the people rose, and each man stood at his tent door and watched Mosheh until he went into the Tent. [9] And it came to be, when Mosheh entered the Tent, that the column of cloud descended and stood at the door of the Tent, and <dn>He</dn> spoke with Mosheh. [10] And all the people saw the column of cloud standing at the Tent door, and all the people rose and bowed themselves, each at his tent door. [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. And he would return to the camp, but his servant Yehoshua son of Nun, a young man, did not leave the Tent.

readings.title: A Plea for Presence and Glory
readings.subtitle: Show Me Your Glory
readings.text: [Exodus 33:12] And Mosheh said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, <dn>You</dn> are saying to me, ‘Bring up this people.’ But <dn>You</dn> have not let me know whom <dn>You</dn> would send with me, though <dn>You</dn> have said, ‘<dn>I</dn> know you by name, and you have also found favour in <dn>My</dn> eyes.’ [13] “And now, please, if <dn>I</dn> have found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, please show me <dn>Your</dn> way, and let me know <dn>You</dn>, so that I find favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes. And consider that this nation is <dn>Your</dn> people.” [14] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>My</dn> Presence does go, and <dn>I</dn> shall give you rest.”</dq> [15] And he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “If <dn>Your</dn> Presence is not going, do not lead us up from here. [16] “For how then shall it be known that I have found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, I and <dn>Your</dn> people, except <dn>You</dn> go with us? Then we shall be distinguished, I and <dn>Your</dn> people, from all the people who are upon the face of the earth.” [17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> do also this word that you have spoken, for you have found favour in <dn>My</dn> eyes, and <dn>I</dn> know you by name.”</dq> [18] And he said, “Please, show me <dn>Your</dn> esteem.” [19] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall cause all <dn>My</dn> goodness to pass before you, and <dn>I</dn> shall proclaim the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before you. And <dn>I</dn> shall favour whom <dn>I</dn> favour, and shall have compassion on whom <dn>I</dn> have compassion.”</dq> [20] But <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“You are unable to see <dn>My</dn> face, for no man sees <dn>Me</dn> and lives.”</dq> [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“See, there is a place by <dn>Me</dn>, and you shall stand on the rock.</dq> [22] <dq>“And it shall be, while <dn>My</dn> esteem passes by, that <dn>I</dn> shall put you in the cleft of the rock and cover you with <dn>My</dn> hand while <dn>I</dn> pass by.</dq> [23] <dq>“Then <dn>I</dn> shall take away <dn>My</dn> hand, and you shall see <dn>My</dn> back, but <dn>My</dn> face shall not be seen.”</dq>

readings.title: The Covenant Renewed
readings.subtitle: New Tablets and the Nature of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Exodus 34:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and <dn>I</dn> shall write on these tablets the words that were on the first tablets which you broke.</dq> [2] <dq>“And be ready in the morning. And you shall come up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and present yourself to <dn>Me</dn> there on the top of the mountain.</dq> [3] <dq>“And let no man come up with you, and let no man be seen throughout all the mountain, and let neither flocks nor herds feed before that mountain.”</dq> [4] And he cut two tablets of stone like the first ones. And Mosheh rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded him, and he took two tablets of stone in his hand. [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> passed before him and proclaimed, <dq>“<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, an <dn>Ěl</dn> compassionate and showing favour, patient, and great in loving-commitment and truth,</dq> [7] <dq>watching over loving-commitment for thousands, forgiving crookedness and transgression and sin, but by no means leaving unpunished, visiting the crookedness of the fathers upon the children and the children’s children to the third and the fourth generation.”</dq> [8] And Mosheh hurried and bowed his head toward the earth, and did obeisance, [9] and said, “If now I have found favour in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, I pray, let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> go on in our midst, even though we are a stiff-necked people. And forgive our crookedness and our sin, and take us as <dn>Your</dn> inheritance.” [10] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am making a covenant. Before all your people <dn>I</dn> am going to do wonders such as have not been done in all the earth, nor in any nation. And all the people among whom you are shall see the work of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For what <dn>I</dn> am doing with you is awesome.</dq> [11] <dq>“Guard what <dn>I</dn> command you today. See, <dn>I</dn> am driving out from before you the Amorite and the Kenaʽanite and the Ḥittite and the Perizzite and the Ḥiwwite and the Yeḇusite.</dq> [12] <dq>“Guard yourself, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land where you are going, lest it be a snare in your midst.</dq> [13] <dq>“But break down their altars, and smash their pillars, and cut down their Ashĕrim –</dq> [14] <dq>for you do not bow yourselves to another mighty one, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, whose Name is Jealous, is a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn> –</dq> [15] <dq>lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they whore after their mighty ones, and slaughter to their mighty ones, and one of them invites you and you eat of his slaughterings,</dq> [16] <dq>and you take of his daughters for your sons, and his daughters whore after their mighty ones, and make your sons whore after their mighty ones.</dq> [17] <dq>“Do not make a moulded mighty one for yourselves.</dq> [18] <dq>“Guard the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you eat unleavened bread, as <dn>I</dn> commanded you, in the appointed time of the month of Aḇiḇ, because in the month of Aḇiḇ you came out from Mitsrayim.</dq> [19] <dq>“All that opens the womb is <dn>Mine</dn>, and every male first-born among your livestock, whether ox or sheep.</dq> [20] <dq>“But the first-born of a donkey you redeem with a lamb. And if you do not redeem him, then you shall break his neck. All the first-born of your sons you redeem. And none shall appear before <dn>Me</dn> empty-handed.</dq> [21] <dq>“Six days you work, but on the seventh day you rest, in ploughing time and in harvest you rest.</dq> [22] <dq>“And you shall perform the Festival of Weeks for yourself, of the first-fruits of wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turn of the year.</dq> [23] <dq>“Three times in the year all your men are to appear before the Master, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl.</dq> [24] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> drive out nations from before you and enlarge your borders, and no one covets your land when you go up to appear before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> three times in the year.</dq> [25] <dq>“Do not offer the blood of <dn>My</dn> slaughtering with leaven, and let not the slaughtering of the Festival of the Passover remain until morning.</dq> [26] <dq>“Bring the first of the first-fruits of your land to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.”</dq> [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Write these words, for according to the mouth of these words <dn>I</dn> have made a covenant with you and with Yisra’ĕl.”</dq> [28] And he was there with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> forty days and forty nights. He did not eat bread and he did not drink water. And <dn>He</dn> wrote on the tablets the Words of the Covenant, the Ten Words. [29] And it came to be, when Mosheh came down from Mount Sinai, while the two tablets of the Witness were in Mosheh’s hand when he came down from the mountain, that Mosheh did not know that the skin of his face shone since he had spoken with <dn>Him</dn>. [30] And Aharon and all the children of Yisra’ĕl looked at Mosheh and saw that the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come near him. [31] And Mosheh called to them, and Aharon and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him, and Mosheh spoke to them. [32] And afterward all the children of Yisra’ĕl came near, and he gave them all the commands which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to him on Mount Sinai. [33] And when Mosheh ended speaking with them, he put a veil on his face. [34] But whenever Mosheh went in before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to speak with <dn>Him</dn>, he removed the veil until he came out. And when he came out and spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl what he had been commanded, [35] the children of Yisra’ĕl saw the face of Mosheh, that the skin of Mosheh’s face shone. And Mosheh put the veil on his face again, until he went in to speak with <dn>Him</dn>.
